newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China-backed stock issues seen flooding pre-97 HK.
newsitem.headline: China-backed stock issues seen flooding pre-97 HK.

text.p: A wave of "red-chip" stock issues will flood Hong Kong in the run-up to the 1997 handover to China with firms seeking easier access to capital in the territory, analysts said on Friday.
As many as 20 China-related firms could issue shares in the British colony before the sovereignty transfer, they said. The handover is in 298 days' time, at midnight on June 30.
"Many Chinese firms are seeking listings in Hong Kong either through H-share listings or by buying shell companies before the 1997 handover," said Michael Ng, an analyst at ASG Brokerage.
"It is easier for them to raise capital in Hong Kong due to relatively huge market liquidity compared with that in China."
Investors had built up a healthy appetite for red chip shares this year and companies were hoping to capitalise on strong market tone, analysts said.
H shares are those of mainland companies listed in Hong Kong. Red chips are Hong Kong incorporated and managed companies with considerable interests in China.
Analysts said there was a rush to list ahead of the handover -- just in case changes lay ahead.

"I'd imagine it is to take advantage of the market buoyancy and to take advantage of current regulations that allow them to list in Hong Kong which may change in June 1997," said Antony Edwards, a director at BZW.
Communist China has not signalled any plans to diverge from its pledge not to interfere in Hong Kong's fiscal administration and to let its capitalist way of life remain unchanged for 50 years.

Although H-shares have been dismal performers this year, one analyst at a Japanese brokerage said the relaxation of austerity measures in China and a recent interest rate cut had improved their perception.
Analysts said the market would welcome a wider variety in H-share issues. The petrochemical industry accounts for more than 50 percent of H-share market capitalisation.

Companies expected to list before the handover include China Eastern Airlines, Shenzhen Expressway, Huling Expressway, Dongfen Motors, and the Hope group -- a food distribution and agribusiness concern.

Other China-backed firms expected to come to market by the end of 1996 or early in 1997 are Anhui Expressway Co, Shandong Xinhua Pharmaceutical and China Resources Beijing Land Ltd, a unit of China Resources Enterprise Ltd.
Investors are also eagerly awaiting the IPO planned by Hong Kong Dragon Airline Ltd (Dragonair).
Merrill Lynch said in a report dated August 28 that Dragonair's flotation plans in early 1997 were still on.
Beijing-controlled and Hong Kong-based satellite owner and operator APT Satellite Co Ltd is also expected to seek a dual listing in Hong Kong and the United States in October.
In the short term, casual wear maker Glorious Sun Enterprises Ltd's 250 million share IPO is expected to be the most eagerly sought after deal.
The issue has been priced at HK$1.60 (20 U.S. cents) per share. The public offering began on Thursday and will run until Tuesday.
With the increasing numbers of China-related firms listing in Hong Kong, analysts said the whole make-up of the Hong Kong stock market was set to change.
"It is obviously becoming structurally risker to invest in the Hong Kong market as a whole than it was a couple of years ago," said one analyst. (US$1 = HK$7.8)
